requirements.title: Character strings have ordered positions and nonnegative length
requirements.source: 7.4.4.1 p1; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF 84, printed 70, lines 3-6.
requirements.definition: Character values are strings: sequences of characters with positions starting at one on the left. Their length counts characters, not source bytes, storage units, or displayed glyphs. LEN is a nonnegative type parameter whose integer kind is processor dependent. A zero-length string is a value, not an invalid declaration. An expression specifying a negative character length has the zero-length interpretation in 7.4.4.2 p5; it is not a counterexample to nonnegative actual LEN.

requirements.oracle: Two run programs check every position in a four-character value and exact LEN/%LEN values for lengths 0, 1 and 4, including an array. Zero-length values are never indexed. The typed integer-kind inquiry remains a pending canonical link. Direct case IDs: S7_4_4_1_001_valid__lengths, S7_4_4_1_001_valid__positions.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No negative twin is inferred from this value definition. These finite witnesses do not enumerate a processor's value set, specify LEN's storage representation, or prove source-byte decoding or graphics. No inquiry is made of an absent optional argument, unallocated deferred-length object, or disassociated deferred-length pointer.

requirements.title: Character representation methods have kind identifiers and inquiries
requirements.source: 7.4.4.1 p2, first four sentences; PDF 84, printed 70, lines 7-11.
requirements.definition: At least one character representation method is required. Each method determines a character value set and is identified by a default-integer KIND parameter value. KIND inquires that value; SELECTED_CHAR_KIND selects by character-type name under its own contract. The existence requirement does not require a nondefault method or support for either named ASCII or ISO_10646 kind. No numerical identifier, ordering of identifiers, byte width, or equality with an integer/real kind is specified.

requirements.oracle: Default-method declarations and DEFAULT selection are required unprofiled run controls. A separate run checks case/trailing-blank equivalence for DEFAULT, ASCII and ISO_10646 and membership of nonnegative results in CHARACTER_KINDS, without instantiating optional kinds. This does not establish full value sets or source mapping. Direct case IDs: S7_4_4_1_002_valid__default_method, S7_4_4_1_002_valid__named_selection.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A selected kind can equal the default kind; no distinct-kind assertion is made without an independent premise. CHARACTER_KINDS order is unspecified. Finite successful declarations or a compiler's familiar numeric kind values do not prove complete repertoire support. Missing method implementation is an observation failure; only genuine optional-method absence can make its qualified witness unavailable.

requirements.title: Representable characters can be members of strings of their method
requirements.source: 7.4.4.1 p2, last sentence; PDF 84, printed 70, lines 11-12.
requirements.definition: A character that the processor can represent in a particular character method can occur in a string of that same method. This concerns data values, including representable control characters; it does not admit every corresponding byte in a source literal, require additional source characters, or allow arbitrary cross-kind conversion. Free/fixed literal admission and source-interface restrictions remain separate.

requirements.oracle: CHAR(0,KIND=KIND('A')) supplies one in-domain character of the required nonempty default method. A run checks its position and count inside a three-character string. It is not identified as NUL, graphic or control, and no ICHAR capacity or byte layout is presumed. Direct case IDs: S7_4_4_1_003_valid__constructed.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The additional-value witness needs processor evidence not yet available. It is not permissible to infer that all integers are valid CHAR inputs, that indices fit a narrower selected integer kind, or that every possible code is graphic. No invalid program or mandated trap follows from the ability to hold a valid value.

accounting.rationale: PDF 84 lines 3-6: subdivide sequence, position, count, parameter kind and nonnegative actual length without equating characters with bytes.
PDF 84 lines 7-12: separate method availability, identifier type, both inquiry references and the last sentence's character-membership effect.
PDF 84 lines 13-16 defines two named character sets/methods; neither definition requires optional method support.

ASCII names the ISO/IEC 646:1991 International Reference Version character set and corresponding method. Its collation is specified in 7.4.4.4 p4; it is not a promise that default character uses that method or source encoding.

ISO 10646 character names the UCS-4 set specified by ISO/IEC 10646 and its corresponding method. This is not a requirement to support ISO_10646, a UTF-8 source/connection rule, or a byte-width inference.
